text:
Maria: Ran a long nsys trace on the TRT-vLLM bridge for the 8k branch. Seeing weird queueing skew where the engine idles then bursts. link: https://s3.redwood-ci/trace/1902468012-out.trc :eyes:
Jon: saw that too — flamegraph shows tons of tiny memcpy + kernel-launch overhead between wrapper->engine. almost like we're issuing per-token launches instead of batched launches.
Kevin: exact numbers from nvprof/ncu?
Maria: nsys summary: total kernel time 3.8s, but 1.9s is _many_ tiny memcpy H2D (cudaMemcpyAsync) fragments, and ~600ms spent in launch overhead (cudaLaunchKernel calls).
Ana: that matches scheduler traces — the scheduler loop is doing a tight handoff: gather_batch -> spawn_engine_call per request instead of aggregating across ready tokens. We set batch_window_ms to 1 in the experiment, which is too aggressive.
Jon: perfetto timeline snippet: https://perfetto.redwood/1902468012 shows back-to-back engine invocations with <200us gaps. Each gap has profiler markers: wrapper:serialize -> wrapper:submit -> engine:begin.
Kevin: hypothesis: wrapper serialization + small host->device memcopies per request are dominating. Two fixes to try: increase batching window, and move KV cache copies into a pre-allocated pinned buffer to coalesce H2D.
Maria: tried increasing batch_window_ms from 1 -> 8 ms in a local run. Results: p50 generation latency dropped 220ms -> 138ms, throughput (tokens/s) up 2.3x. Early numbers only but consistent across 3 runs.
perf-bot: perf regression check: baseline 220ms (p50), current 138ms (p50). No test flakiness detected. :white_check_mark:
Jon: good. Also noticed KV warmup churn: first 6 tokens cause repeated KV writes due to naive attach logic. For long contexts that warmup cost amortizes, but for short prompts it's painful.
Ana: code patch proposal: change KV attach to single batched H2D per request where possible. Pseudocode:
```
// before
for each shard in kv_shards:
  cudaMemcpyAsync(shard->buf, local_copy, size)
  submit()

// after
coalesce_local -> pinned_buf
cudaMemcpyAsync(device_kv, pinned_buf, total_size)
submit()
```
Kevin: also consider using cudaGraph capture for the common path (single-engine call + kv attach) to remove kernel launch overhead. We tested graph capture in an isolated benchmark: launch overhead reduced ~60% for the steady hot path.
Maria: tried enabling graph capture for small batches — tricky with dynamic sequence length, but for fixed prefix workloads it's promising. Need safety fallback when shapes diverge.
Jon: another micro observation: scheduler uses a spin-wait on a mutex around the ready queue leading to CPU-side jitter. We should replace with an MPMC lock-free queue or use condition variable with eventfd to avoid busy spinning.
Ana: I prototyped switching to eventfd notify — CPU utilization down ~12% and jitter reduced (seen in perf samples). Not a silver bullet but helps under high concurrency.
Kevin: for the next run, we should: 1) enable pinned KV coalescing, 2) bump batch_window_ms to 6–8ms, 3) enable cudaGraph for stable shapes, 4) replace spin lock with eventfd notify.
Maria: scheduled a longer nsys run across 3 instance shapes (A100, H100, L4) tonight. Uploading traces to same bucket: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1902468012-batch-window-sweep/ — will share perfetto links when available.
Jon: can you also include a nsight timeline with CPU stacks so we can pinpoint wrapper-side hotspots?
Maria: yes — will capture with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu -o out.trc -- python -m vllm.runserver` and include perf records.
deploy-bot: Canary (canary-3) running patch branch br/190246-kv-coalesce as of 2026-03-17T02:45Z
Kevin: small ask — add a metric for "engine-launch-count" per second to console so we can detect regressions (spikes when we regress to per-token launches).
Ana: added draft dashboard panel in console: engine-launch-rate & kv-h2d-rate. Will iterate once we have more traces.
Maria: thanks all — next update after long trace completes. If anyone wants early access to raw nsys files ping me. :thumbsup:
